name: Coconut-Parsnip Soup with Lemongrass and Ginger

ingredients.name: fresh, or dried makrut lime leaves
kosher salt, plus more to taste

instructions.primary_message: Peel and roughly chop the parsnips. Chop the yellow onion. Pick the cilantro leaves and tender stems from the thick stems and chop them. Mince the garlic. Stem, seed, and finely chop the jalapeño pepper. Shake the full-fat coconut milk in the can. Keep the fresh frozen until you use it. Chop the toasted cashews.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 medium parsnips
½ large yellow onion
¼ cup fresh cilantro leaves, tender stems
3 large cloves garlic
1 jalapeño pepper
2 (383 g) cans full-fat coconut milk
2 fresh, or dried makrut lime leaves
Toasted cashews

instructions.primary_message: In a large pot, heat coconut oil over medium heat until shimmering. Add parsnips and onion. Cook, stirring occasionally, until onions soften, about 5 minutes. Stir in chopped galangal or ginger, cilantro, garlic, and jalapeño, and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.

Stir in coconut milk, broth, galangal or ginger pieces, lemongrass, makrut lime leaves, and salt. Bring mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer. Cook, covered, until parsnips are tender, about 20 minutes.

Off-heat, use a slotted spoon to remove and discard galangal or ginger pieces, lemongrass, and makrut lime leaves. Carefully transfer parsnip mixture to a blender. Blend, in batches if necessary, on medium-high speed until smooth, about 1 minute. (Alternatively, blend soup in pot with an immersion blender until smooth.) Season soup with additional salt to taste. Divide soup between serving bowls. Top with cilantro leaves and cashews. Serve with lime wedges on the side.

schema_metadata.keywords: parsnip soup, creamy soup, vegetable soup, coconut soup, tom kha, tom kha ghai, coconut parsnip soup, puréed soup

description: This creamy parsnip soup recipe, inspired by Thai tom kha, is made with coconut milk, lemongrass, galangal (or ginger), and makrut lime leaves. It's comforting enough for winter but light and bright enough to take you into spring.
notes:
Optional substitutions: yellow onion → white onion; galangal → ginger; homemade chicken stock → store-bought unsalted chicken or vegetable broth

Notes: Galangal, lemongrass, and makrut lime leaves can be found at many Asian grocery stores.

Make-ahead and storage: Leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days or frozen for up to 2 months.
author: Kayla Simone Fowler
